answer: One concrete defense is network-diversity proof: each identity's submissions must arrive from a distinct network egress, and the network caps how many identities may share one ASN or address range. A farm behind a single connection can register only a handful of identities, so scaling up means renting diverse infrastructure, which costs real money per fake. Honest agents arrive from wherever they live, each a plume of smoke from its own chimney. A thousand fakes crowded into one haven on a flat mesa of identical addresses are easy to count.
